exclusion_evidence: The eleven development recording groups and the TrackNet game1 diagnostic stay excluded with their recorded raw/prepared SHA-256 identities. Scoreboards and venues in the decoded frames of the five new sources name player pairs and events that differ from every development cue and from the six historical v1 gallery/stress matches; no new downloaded or prepared SHA-256 equals an excluded identity. Some individual players recur in other matches. This comparison is by visible match identity and file hash, not by a pixel search of the development footage.
limitations: These are resized copies of the parent clips, not independent footage or camera-native 256x144 video. They share every limitation of the parent inventory.
Resized images do not have the parent RGB. Labels or outputs made on the parent join by frame index and integer PTS, with image coordinates scaled by the size ratio.

Lob and live ball occlusion are not confirmed in any clip, and a serve is confirmed in one. The review sampled forty frames per clip plus selected crops, so an unlisted category is unreviewed rather than absent; required_gallery_ready stays false.

gallery-v2-04-03 and gallery-v2-04-04 each end with thirteen frames after a hard cut to a player close-up, and gallery-v2-04-03 opens under a fading transition graphic. The ranges are kept as requested; calibration and tracking on those frames are expected to fail and must be reported, not removed.
gallery-v2-02-03 and gallery-v2-02-04 use a lower, wider camera with spectators in the foreground, and in the Beijing clips the near player partly leaves the bottom of the frame at times.

The Indian Wells 2012 source is a watermarked third-party re-upload, not an authorized publisher version; no authorized upload with the same timeline was identified. Its direct stream returned HTTP 403 twice, so its 1080p AVC stream was downloaded through yt-dlp's HLS route.

All five sources are edited highlight videos. Sources offer up to 2160p for one video and 1080p for the rest; the 1920x1080 AVC stream of each was downloaded so the cohort has one resolution and codec. Encoded frame rates are 25, 50 and about 59.94 per second; only integer PTS define time.

No ball 2D, bounce, contact, calibration, landing or airborne XYZ truth exists for these clips. The 192 hit/bounce labels of the historical v1 gallery belong to other footage and are not reused; new source-bound labels are required.
Detector checkpoint training overlap is unknown. Separation from this project's development recordings does not establish detector training independence.

Footage, download metadata, review images and detector weights stay private. No redistribution grant is verified. A later download can produce different bytes; exact reproduction needs the preserved source files and the recorded PyAV build.
Twenty user-selected highlight ranges from five professional singles matches are a convenience sample, not a population sample.
selection_rule: Every clip of the parent inventory, derived frame for frame at 256x144. No clip, frame or range was selected, dropped or altered, and no model output was read. Parent selection rule: User-selected replacement gallery: twenty exact source-second ranges across five YouTube highlight videos. Each source's requested ranges were fixed before its acquisition; all twenty ranges were specified before final input freeze and inference. Every requested range is retained unaltered under the declared endpoint rule, including two ranges that end after a camera cut. Source-only review (contact sheets of forty frames per clip, adjacent-frame change scan, global-shift measurement and cropped opening frames) recorded view, format, camera motion and cuts before any detector or lifter output existed. No clip was moved, shortened, replaced or dropped.
